page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor configuration includes 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, supported by a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.g6.xlarge sits primarily in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy workloads. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 25% of benchmarked hardware. Similarly, memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached operations fall into the bottom 25%, although the Passmark memory score achieves an average rating. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, also register in the lower percentiles, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression dropping to the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource density make this instance a predictable option for workloads that do not require high-performance computing or local storage. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio is suitable for standard general-purpose applications. Appropriate workloads include light web serving, basic database operations, development environments, and general-purpose utility tasks that can operate within the 2 Gbps network baseline and do not demand intensive multi-threaded processing.
